questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I'm studying an area studies, I wanted to choose a location about that area as well as a location where I was able to practice the language I'm studying for my degree.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We received many emails about different activities and registration and it was a bit overwhelming. But I think we had the information we needed through these.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We all got assigned a student volunteer. She helped me with information even before I arrived and was also very kind to help me with all my questions when I arrived as well. She always was quick to reply and had very elaborated answers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We were able to choose some different dorms (single rooms/shared rooms).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a common room for the whole building where you could cook but I never used as it seemed a bit inconvenient. I don't think it was used that often in general.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The dorm (Shui-Yuan) is a very cheap option close the campus. They do have some rules but in general these are easy to abide by I think. However, since I had a single person room and you in general didn't engage with your neighbours, I found it a bit lonely at times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course selection system at NTU is quite different from the one at UCPH. It takes place in several stages where the portal is open for you to sign up. After each stage you can check your results for a limited time. If you didn't get the course you wanted at first, you can try signing up again. In the end, if you're still unsuccesful, you can either message the teacher or showing up in person on the first day of class and ask if it's possible to join. I found that it often is. However, if the class is really popular, it might not be.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were some information online but I used my student volunteer a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first, I was not and I found this very stressful. I managed to join to other courses, I iniatially didn't get by either messaging the professor or showing up in class. As I thought it would be very difficult to join, I was quite suprised that I managed to join that easily.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I'd say you shouldn't stress too much even if you don't get the courses at first as it is often possible to join after, even if it says online that the course is full. Often the teacher is willing to let you join, at least in my experience. Also, I'd recommend to test out more classes in the first week and decide afterwards which one's to join or not. I perhaps chose my classes a bit too quickly since I was scared that I wouldn't have enough credits. I wished I'd taken more time to consider the different classes more.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses only for MA students and also courses that were open for both BA and MA students together.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I didn't find the teaching style that different but since your grade is not only based on a final exam but also often both class participation, midterms as well as presentations, the focus might be a bit different in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Seminar on East Asia News
Enhancing Chinese
General Chinese 
Introduction to Translation Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Even if you're major is not about Chinese, I'd still recommend you to enroll in the Chinese language courses if possible. I think the courses were very well taught and I learned a lot.

questions.answer: I think I had a good idea of the price levels already so I was not really surprised.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Through my scholarship we got to participate in events where we were matched with local families with whom we did activities with. I also was invited to dinner and trips with these families later on.

I also participated in a cultural exchange program (ICL) in which I was matched with a local student and a school class in a city in Taiwan. Each week we had a skype session where I shared Danish culture and traditions with them and they shared Taiwanese culture and traditions with me. I also got to visit them one time.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the ones I mentioned above were great. I think they were some great opportunities to get to meet local people and experience local culture. Although I myself did not have time for clubs or assocations, I knew some fellow students who participated in these and they liked it very much. This is also a way to meet other people and to connect with local students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I think Taiwan has a lot of nice nature spots, and I'd recommend to go visit these. Besides, Taiwan is not very big so it's quite easy and fast to go to other cities for a short visit during the weekend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since I've been on exchange before in East Asia as well, I found the adjustment quite easy and to happen quite quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think joining events, clubs or associations are good options to meet local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found the local people to be very helpful and friendly. I liked that a lot. Also, there is a lot of trust and I never felt unsafe. I also left my stuff at cafes when I went to the toilet and I never feared that my stuff would get stolen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Firstly, in the beginning it can seem quite overwelming with all the things needed to be done. But don't worry, it'll all work out after some time. During this I think it's important to consult wiht fellow students who are also going or with your student volunteer. This perhaps can lessen your worry. 

Secondly, try to move outside your comfort zone. I think it’s easy just to make friends with fellow Danes or other Europeans. I did that myself to an extent. But I think it’s also important to try and make friends with local people or people from very different cultures than your own. I think this was very giving and a way to widen your horizon and learn more about different cultures and people.

Lastly, make sure to enjoy it. A semester goes by very quickly, much quicker than you might expect. I think I myself spent too much time worriying about the academic part and didn’t have time to do other stuff. I realized in the end that I could’ve prioritized a bit differently without it affecting my grades.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The course selection system can seem quite intimidating at first and caused me a lot of stress. I think a elaborated guide for this would have been very nice as it in the end turned out to not be that complicated or difficult as I first found it to be.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met at lot of different people and got to share my own culture as well as learning about others. I also got to improve and use my Chinese language skills a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think balancing studying, being social and also experience the country you were in was the most challenging. I often felt like I was missing out on either of them if I prioritized the others.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
